#+title: Transparent build-station production

Run the normal commands:

#+begin_src sh
./bin/bl build
./bin/bl build --force
./bin/bl self-build --out ./bl-release
#+end_src

Managed preparation uses Nix's configured remote builders. The daemon owns
transport and credentials; each command uses the same policy. A missing or
unreachable builder produces a preparation error and preserves the selection.

Beam Lisp backend descriptions compile to standard Nix configuration.
See [[file:nix-codec.org][Source-owned backend descriptions]] for the declaration and module factory.
Nix owns builder selection through that configuration. A local worker,
an SSH builder, and a service such as nixbuild.net consume the same recipes.
Configure transport, authentication and supported system features on the client.

For a managed host using this repository's module, supply a local build
description to the module factory. Addresses, credentials, host keys and
capacity belong to the operator's deployment, outside Beam Lisp:

#+begin_src nix
imports = [ (beam-lisp.lib.artifact-workstation {
  description = ./build-backend.bl;
}) ];
#+end_src

The =.bl= description and adjacent generated =.nix= projection define the
backend kind, Nix settings, builders and optional evaluation endpoint. Compile
and check it with =scripts/compile-build-backends.bl=. The module verifies its
Source digest before applying the policy. Use =lib.build-backend= for a plain
Nix policy module, or =lib.artifact-workstation= for the managed resource policy.

Declare actual builder capabilities explicitly. Bounded Linux workers require
=kvm=; the selected builder must provide it. Provider host keys and credentials
belong in deployment configuration or CI secrets.

Remote Nix builders place realization on the station. They do not place Nix
evaluation there. Moving evaluation requires an operator-provided endpoint
with that capability; an ssh-ng store credential alone cannot run commands.

Generic hosts can use nixosModules.artifacts and set
services.beam-lisp-artifacts.buildDescription. The generic module retains its
legacy buildStation adapter for existing deployments; the two cannot select a
backend together. Set =maxJobs = 0= to use builders configured by another
module. Station daemon/worker resource limits are configured on
the station itself; client limits describe a separate execution domain.

The existing nixosModules.artifact-workstation export remains a module, but
requires services.beam-lisp-artifacts.buildDescription from local Source. It
refuses a missing description.

* Optional evaluation placement

A Source description can additionally supply =:evaluation=:

#+begin_src clojure
:evaluation {"storeUri" "ssh-ng://builder@build.example.invalid"
             "transport" ["ssh" "operator@build.example.invalid" "{endpoint}"]}
#+end_src

These are examples, not Beam Lisp defaults. The local operator owns addresses,
credentials and SSH host-key policy. The transport must permit running the
immutable endpoint sent with the platform. An existing forced ssh-ng key does
not grant that capability. Omit =:evaluation= for a store-only station.
The client copies the platform and captured inputs and invokes its finite recipe
endpoint. It imports the resulting derivation, checks its declared output, and
asks the configured Nix daemon to retrieve the completed product through its
authenticated remote builder. Local build jobs are disabled for this step.
The retained output must match before remote root cleanup is acknowledged.
A configured endpoint failure never falls back to Work.

The NixOS module emits this local description as
=/etc/beam-lisp/build-station.json=. It is host configuration, never project
input or a field in an artifact request. No resident service is required.
An existing =$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/beam-lisp/build-station.json= takes precedence;
=XDG_CONFIG_HOME= defaults to =~/.config=. Install its evaluation transport
from the checked Source description with:

#+begin_src sh
mkdir -p ~/.config/beam-lisp
python3 scripts/build-backend.py --description /path/to/build-backend.bl \
  --station-out ~/.config/beam-lisp/build-station.json
#+end_src

An explicitly selected =--description= must exist. A configured transport
failure preserves the request for diagnosis and does not select another host.
Unacknowledged outputs remain rooted under the station user's
=$XDG_CACHE_HOME/beam_lisp/station/TICKET= for recovery. Each request has its own
root, including concurrent requests for identical products.

Source capture reads the local checkout. Bootstrap coordinator selection also
runs on the client. The endpoint places SDK, native, application and portable
recipe evaluation on the operator's station. Store-only providers use ordinary
client evaluation and Nix remote realization; no operator shell endpoint is
needed for that route.

Nix routing and SSH settings cross managed process boundaries through the
finite client environment: =NIX_CONFIG=, =NIX_SSHOPTS=, =NIX_USER_CONF_FILES=,
=NIX_CONF_DIR=, =SSH_AUTH_SOCK= and =XDG_CONFIG_HOME=. Prefer references to private
configuration files for credentials. These settings are runtime policy,
separate from product inputs and artifact requests. See
[[file:ci-worker.org][CI worker configuration]] for nixbuild.net setup.
